subject: Modularization & migration choices for Healix packaging
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@healix.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Huang <mike.huang@healix.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Question: migration paths & packaging for mid-stage rollout

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the notes internally and have a follow-up set of questions focused on packaging and migration: Healix is looking to move from trial seats to a staged production rollout across three product teams over Q4. We need clarity on:

- A recommended migration pattern (big-bang vs staged) for minimizing latency/regression risk
- How feature bundles are treated during a tier upgrade (do we keep entitlements, prorate, or remap?)
- Discounting/commit levers if we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity for two teams now and the third team later
- Any constraints for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) during an incremental migration

I attached our migration workbook (Healix_Migration_requests.xlsx) with per-team usage curves and target go-live windows. Can you outline 2–3 concrete options with high-level cost and timeline implications? Also want an idea of typical discounts for staged commitments vs. immediate full-commit.

Appreciate a short write-up or a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Head of Platform, Healix.ai
Attachments: Healix_Migration_requests.xlsx
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@healix.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: migration paths & packaging for mid-stage rollout

Sara — thanks for the workbook, looks clean and helpful. I pulled together three pragmatic paths based on similar mid-market migrations:

Option A — Modular staged migration (recommended)
- Bring team A onto dedicated capacity first, keep teams B/C on hosted for 8–12 weeks.
- Entitlements: we preserve feature flags for each team; billing moves per-team when they cutover.
- Discounting: tiered commit discounts apply per committed pool; we can ladder 10% on first commit, +3% when you commit an additional team within 90 days.
- Pros: lowest disruption, easy rollback. Cons: slightly higher total spend during overlap.

Option B — Fast consolidated commit
- Commit capacity for A+B now, migrate both in 4 weeks, add C later.
- Entitlements: full remap onto consolidated plan; prorated credits applied for partial months.
- Discounting: deeper up-front discount (we can discuss a one-time incentive for consolidated N+ seats).

Option C — Pilot + burst credits
- Keep teams on hosted; use burst reserved capacity as needed during peak windows.
- Useful if usage is spiky and you want to avoid immediate contracts.

Technical note: for private deployments there are two constraints we flag: (1) longer lead time for VPC peering and KMS integration, (2) model quantization profiles may differ between hosted and private GPU types which can cause small latency delta. Priyom (cc'd) can add specifics.

Next steps: I can draft a short proposal (PDF) showing cost curves for the three options and a recommended timeline. Would you prefer that or a quick call? We can also include a sample DocuSign for staged commitments.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Sara — quick add from the AE side based on what typically helps procurement move faster: 

- Offer a 60-day early-termination credit for teams that commit but need to swap timelines; reduces legal friction.
- Consider a modular bundle: Core Inference + KV-cache addon + Observability pack. You can opt teams into different addon sets while keeping the core commitment pooled.
- Pricing mechanics we usually propose: base commit + per-token overage at a fixed rate; we can cap overage for the first 6 months to give you predictability.

If you want, we can include a “migration grace” clause in the SOW that allows one free seat reallocation between teams during the first 90 days. That often helps alignment across product managers.

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@healix.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: migration paths & packaging for mid-stage rollout

Looping in a brief technical perspective from Product/Optimize: 

- Entitlement mapping: we can preserve per-team prompt sets and instruction-tuning configs when moving between hosted and dedicated, but there is a manual step for KV-cache warmup. Plan ~48–72 hours of degraded perf as caches populate unless you pre-warm with historical prefixes.
- Quantization & model variants: if you move to on-prem GPU types we recommend a compatibility window where both variants are run in parallel for a week and we measure quality drift. The Optimize team can provide suggested quant profiles to reduce cost with minimal quality loss.
- Billing split: we recommend issuing per-team sub-accounts under the dedicated pool so usage is traceable; Redwood can export token-level CSV daily for your internal chargeback.

Discount note: from a product standpoint we prefer to see baseline usage for 30 days before applying multi-team ladder discounts because it reduces churn risk. We can encode that as a 30-day usage verification in the contract, then backdate discounts if targets are met.

Priyom Das
Senior PM, Redwood Optimize
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@healix.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: migration paths & packaging for mid-stage rollout

Thanks everyone — this is helpful and aligns with what the product teams wanted to hear. Based on your notes we want to proceed with Option A (Modular staged migration) with the following asks: 

- Drafted proposal/pdf with cost curves comparing Option A vs B for transparency (we tend to benchmark both)
- A SOW clause for one free seat reallocation within 90 days and a 30-day usage verification step before ladder discounts kick in
- Estimated dates: Team A flip week of Sep 20, Team B aim Oct 25, Team C Jan 10 (tentative)
- DocuSign-ready quote for the first commitment (team A, 12-month) and a separate addendum for future teams

If you can send the proposal and DocuSign this week, we can route to procurement (contracts@healix.ai). Appreciate the pragmatic guidance — we’ll review the proposal and circle back with procurement redlines if any.
